findings.text: Physical and virtual timer enable checks consult a sanitized timer control view for the vcpu and select local handling when the respective shifted enable is present, otherwise they request forwarding of read and write.
A vcpu counts as a nested NV2 guest exactly when its HCR EL2 view has E2H plus NV2 plus NV asserted while TGE plus NV1 are clear.

The EL1 NV physical and virtual timer redirection checks handle locally unless both hold: the vcpu satisfies the nested NV2 guest predicate and the corresponding NV redirection enable is set in CNTHCTL EL2. When both hold they request forwarding of read and write.
The CPTR TTA check reads CPTR EL2, converts it to a CPACR EL1 view when E2H is clear, then requests forwarding when the TTA bit is set and local handling otherwise.

The MDCR HPMN check derives a PMU counter index from the faulting instruction: for direct event type and counter registers it decodes fields of the encoding, for multiplexed selector based registers it reads the selector register. Hypervisor owned counters request forwarding including host EL0, others handle locally.
The HCR NV without NVTGE check requests forwarding when HCR EL2 indicates nested virtualization is active and HCRX EL2 does not indicate NVTGE, otherwise it handles locally.

A constant table indexed by condition identifier minus a base offset dispatches seven complex conditions for timer enables, timer NV redirection, CPTR TTA, MDCR HPMN and HCR NV without NVTGE to their respective checker routines.

Trap configuration is a 64 bit value overlaid with a bitfield record holding coarse trap identifier, fine trap identifier, bit number, polarity, fine filter, system register index, a reserved zero region and a must be zero bit.

Field widths are ten bits for coarse trap identifier, four bits for fine trap identifier, five bits for fine filter and ten bits for system register index, with six bits for bit number, one for polarity, twenty seven reserved and one must be zero filling the 64 bit word.

Encoding mapping entries associate a start encoding and an end encoding with a trap configuration value and the definition source line, allowing single registers and contiguous ranges to share one trap description.
Two table constructors create mapping entries: one records an explicit start and end encoding with a coarse trap identifier, the other records a single encoding by using it for both bounds.

The boot constant encoding table assigns coarse trap categories to EL1 and EL0 identification, cache maintenance, TLB maintenance by scope and shareability, address translation, memory management, error records, pointer authentication keys, performance monitors and debug encodings, with performance counter registers sharing combined TPM categories.

The same table assigns the nested virtualization category to a broad set of EL2 registers, stage two translation and TLB operations and aliased EL02 or EL12 ranges, with narrow exceptions for selected NV timer controls, stack pointer, exception state and context number registers that use specialized NV related categories.
Invoking the MDCR HPMN helper for an encoding outside the expected performance monitor event and counter families raises a bug assertion against the owning VM and then selects local handling.
External bug assertion helper owned by another dossier and referenced by the PMU trap helper.
